Frozen, citable copies of these materials are archived on Zenodo. The version cited in the article is v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23266798), which updates the figures archived in v1.0.0; the analyses and results are unchanged.

title: Supplemental Materials
text:
Analysis Reports
Each report is a rendered Quarto document containing the complete analysis code and output: model specifications and priors, full parameter tables, the group and interaction effects reported in the article, figures, and posterior predictive checks. The corresponding source files (.qmd) are available in the source folder.



Report
Description




Verbal Feature Analyses
Bayesian mixed models for word count, seven LIWC-22 categories, and LLM-rated sentiment (Table 2, Figure 1)


Vocal Feature Analyses
Bayesian mixed models for nine prosodic and voice quality features (Table 3, Figure 2)


Visual Feature Analyses
Bayesian mixed models for five facial action units and four head pose and motion features (Table 4, Figure 3)

title: Supplemental Materials
text:
Data Availability
The deidentified behavioral features and model covariates analyzed in this work are openly available (CC BY 4.0). Each file has one row per participant and task, and participants are identified only by arbitrary codes (P001–P092) that are shared across files. The codebook describes every column.



File
Contents
Size





verbal.csv
Word count, LIWC-22 categories, and sentiment ratings
31 KB



vocal.csv
Prosodic and voice quality features
37 KB



visual.csv
Facial action unit intensities and head pose and motion
39 KB




The complete v1.1.0 archive (data, code, and reports) can also be downloaded as a single file from Zenodo:  Download all (ZIP, 5.9 MB)
These files, together with the analysis source code, are sufficient to reproduce every model, table, and figure in the analysis reports. The video, audio, and transcript data cannot be shared because they contain identifiable protected health information. The other participant-level demographic and clinical measures summarized in Table 1 are not shared to protect participant privacy; the Sample Demographics report shows the code used to produce that table.

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)




Code
read_features <- function(modality) {
  read.csv(file.path("..", "data", paste0(modality, ".csv"))) |>
    as_tibble()
}

id_cols <- c("participant", "source", "ptsd", "demo_age", "demo_sex", "demo_nonwhite", "task")

df_features <-
  read_features("verbal") |>
  full_join(read_features("vocal"), by = id_cols) |>
  full_join(read_features("visual"), by = id_cols) |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(ptsd, levels = c(1, 0), labels = c("PTSD", "Control")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("Account", "Impact"))
  )

# Feature labels, display precision, and modality, in table order
spec <- tribble(
  ~var,          ~label,                                  ~digits, ~modality,
  "WC",          "Total Word Count",                      0,       "Verbal",
  "i",           "1st Person Singular Pronouns (%)",      2,       "Verbal",

  "emo_neg",     "Negative Emotion Words (%)",            2,       "Verbal",

title: Behavioral Feature Descriptives
Behavioral Feature Descriptives
text:
Table S1


Code
cell_stats <-
  df_features |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(spec$var), names_to = "var") |>
  summarize(
    .by = c(var, group, task),
    m = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    s = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  left_join(spec, by = "var") |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.*f (%.*f)", digits, m, digits, s))

table_s1 <-
  cell_stats |>
  select(modality, var, label, group, task, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(group, task), values_from = cell, names_sep = "_") |>
  arrange(match(var, spec$var)) |>
  select(modality, label, PTSD_Account, Control_Account, PTSD_Impact, Control_Impact)

n_group <- df_features |> distinct(participant, group) |> count(group) |> deframe()

table_s1 |>
  gt(groupname_col = "modality", rowname_col = "label") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Table S1",
    subtitle = "Means and Standard Deviations for Behavioral Features by Group and Task"
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Trauma Account", columns = c(PTSD_Account, Control_Account)) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Impact Statement", columns = c(PTSD_Impact, Control_Impact)) |>
  cols_label(
    PTSD_Account = sprintf("PTSD (n = %d)", n_group[["PTSD"]]),
    Control_Account = sprintf("Control (n = %d)", n_group[["Control"]]),
    PTSD_Impact = sprintf("PTSD (n = %d)", n_group[["PTSD"]]),
    Control_Impact = sprintf("Control (n = %d)", n_group[["Control"]])
  ) |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = -label) |>
  tab_source_note(md(paste(
    "*Note.* Values are *M* (*SD*) in each feature's original units.",
    "LIWC-22 categories are percentages of total words.",
    "Sentiment is the LLM-predicted rating of each transcript (1 = very negative, 7 = very positive).",
    "Action unit (AU) values are OpenFace intensity estimates (0–5) averaged over frames.",
    "Head pose values are mean rotations and head motion values are the root mean square of",
    "successive frame-to-frame differences in rotation, in radians.",
    "The models analyze LIWC percentages divided by 100 and AU intensities divided by 5."
  )))
